title: Ethics on the Job: Autonomy, End of Life and Accountability

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already respect patients' choices and put their welfare first. As a PCP, the decisions get harder:

  1. Use the four principles to think through a dilemma
  2. Apply capacity, consent and substitute decisions on real calls
  3. Handle end of life, resuscitation decisions, and your own mistakes

Textbook: Chapter 5, PDF pages 278–310
slides.say: Welcome to the ethics lesson. As EMRs, you already respect patients' choices and put their welfare first, and last lesson covered the law behind that. Ethics goes further: doing the right thing when the law gives no clear answer. As a PCP you'll meet harder versions of these moments: more treatments that need consent, more drugs that can go wrong, and harder talks with families. Today we'll cover the four principles of medical ethics; capacity, consent and substitute decision makers on real calls; and end of life, resuscitation decisions, and owning your mistakes.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到伦理课。作为 EMR，你已经会尊重病人的选择、把病人福祉放在首位，上节课讲了这背后的法律。伦理更进一步：在法律没有明确答案时，做正确的事。作为 PCP，你会遇到这些时刻更难的版本：需要同意的治疗更多，可能出错的药更多，和家属的谈话也更难。今天讲医学伦理的四项原则；决策能力、同意和替代决策者在实际出车中怎么用；以及临终、复苏决定，和如何面对自己的差错。

slides.title: Four principles, one question
slides.body:
PrincipleIn plain words
AutonomyCapable patients decide for themselves
BeneficenceDo what's best for the patient
Non-maleficenceFirst, do no harm
JusticeTreat like cases alike; share resources fairly

When they clash, ask: what is in this patient's best interest?

The book prints "nonmalfeasance"; the standard term is non-maleficence.
slides.say: Ethics is about right and wrong, duties, and ideal professional behaviour. Morality is the personal code you get from family, culture or religion. On a call, the patient's interests come before your own beliefs; that's your fiduciary duty, the trust the public places in you. A common framework, principlism, uses four principles. Autonomy: capable patients decide for themselves. Beneficence: do what's best for the patient. Non-maleficence: first, do no harm. Justice: treat similar cases alike and share resources fairly. These principles can clash, and they won't hand you an answer. When you're stuck, ask: what is in this patient's best interest?
slides.sayZh: 伦理讲的是对与错、责任和理想的职业行为。道德是你从家庭、文化或宗教中得来的个人准则。出车时，病人的利益优先于你自己的信念，这是你的受托责任，也就是公众对你的信任。常用的框架叫原则主义，有四项原则。自主：有能力的病人自己做决定。行善：做对病人最好的事。不伤害：首先，不造成伤害。公正：相似的情况相同对待，公平分配资源。这些原则会互相冲突，也不会直接给你答案。卡住的时候，就问：什么最符合这位病人的利益？

slides.title: Capacity: understand and appreciate
slides.body:
Understandthe condition and the options
Appreciatewhat each choice will lead to
Changeswith illness, drugs, alcoholreassess often
  • Presume capacity until shown otherwise
  • Capable patients may refuse even life-saving care
  • Capable for a simple treatment ≠ capable for a complex one
slides.say: Last lesson gave you a practical capacity checklist; this chapter adds the core idea. Capacity has two parts: the patient can understand information about their condition and options, and can appreciate the consequences of choosing, or not choosing. Someone may understand perfectly yet not appreciate what will happen to them; that's not full capacity. Start by presuming capacity, and remember a capable patient may refuse even life-saving care. Capacity changes with illness, medication, alcohol or drugs, so reassess during the call. It's also specific: a patient may be capable of agreeing to oxygen, but not to a more complex treatment.
slides.sayZh: 上节课给了你一份实用的决策能力清单，这一章补上核心概念。决策能力有两部分：能理解关于病情和选项的信息；能领会作出选择或不作选择的后果。有人完全听懂了，却没意识到自己会面临什么后果，那就不算完全有能力。先推定病人有能力，并记住有能力的病人可以拒绝哪怕是救命的治疗。能力会随疾病、药物、酒精或毒品变化，所以出车中要反复评估。能力也是针对具体事情的：病人可能有能力同意吸氧，却没有能力同意一项更复杂的治疗。

slides.title: Valid consent: capable, informed, voluntary
slides.body:
Capableor a legal substitute decides
Informedwhat a reasonable person would want to know
Voluntaryno coercion or manipulation
  • Why it's needed, and the alternatives
  • Benefits, real risks and side effects
  • What happens without it; your recommendation
  • Time for questions

Emergency + incapable = presumed consent (Chapter 4 called it "implied").
slides.say: For consent to be ethically valid, the patient must be capable, or a legal substitute decision maker consents; the consent must be informed; and it must be voluntary. How much is informed? What a reasonable person in the patient's place would expect: why the treatment is needed, the options, the benefits, the real risks and side effects, what happens without it, and why you recommend it. Then allow time for questions. In an emergency, when the patient can't decide, consent is presumed and you err on the side of life. Note the wording: chapter four called this implied consent; here, implied means consent shown by action.
slides.sayZh: 同意要在伦理上有效：病人必须有能力，或由合法的替代决策者同意；必须是知情的；必须是自愿的。讲多少才算知情？以处在病人位置的合理人会期望知道的为准：为什么需要这项治疗、有哪些选择、好处、实际风险和副作用、不做会怎样、你为什么推荐。然后留时间让他提问。紧急情况下病人无法决定时，推定同意，偏向保命。注意用词：第四章把这叫默示同意；而这一章里，默示同意指用行动表示的同意。

slides.q: A man with sudden weakness on one side can repeat back what you said about a possible stroke and the care you're offering. But he insists nothing bad will happen if he waits until tomorrow. What's true?
options: He's capable, because he understood the information
His capacity is in doubt: he doesn't appreciate the consequences
Capacity only matters for unconscious patients
He's capable, because he's calm and polite
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A man with sudden weakness on one side can repeat back what you said about a possible stroke and the care you're offering. But he insists nothing bad will happen if he waits until tomorrow. What's true? A, he's capable, because he understood the information. B, his capacity is in doubt, because he doesn't appreciate the consequences. C, capacity only matters for unconscious patients. D, he's capable, because he's calm and polite. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：一位突然一侧无力的男士，能复述你讲的「可能是中风」以及你提供的处置，但他坚持认为等到明天也不会有事。下面哪句对？A 他有能力，因为他听懂了信息；B 他的能力存疑，因为他没有领会后果；C 只有昏迷病人才需要考虑能力；D 他有能力，因为他平静又礼貌。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Capacity needs both understanding the facts and appreciating the consequences. He can repeat the facts but doesn't see what could happen to him, so keep explaining, reassess, and consult direct medical control. A forgets the second part of capacity. C is wrong: capacity matters most for awake patients making choices. D is wrong because a calm manner tells you nothing about appreciation.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。决策能力要求既理解事实，又领会后果。他能复述事实，却看不到自己可能面临什么，所以要继续解释、重新评估，并咨询直接医疗指导。A 忘了能力的第二部分；C 错，能力恰恰对清醒、要作选择的病人最重要；D 错，态度平静说明不了他是否领会后果。

slides.title: Persuade; never coerce or manipulate
slides.body:
Persuasionhonest concern and reasonsethical
Coercionthreatsnot ethical
Manipulationscare tactics, exaggerationnot ethical

A good goal doesn't justify a bad method.
slides.say: Sometimes a patient who clearly needs hospital care says no, and you negotiate. There's an ethical line here. Persuasion is fine: honest concern and reasons, like, your blood pressure worries me, and I'd feel much better if a doctor saw you today. Coercion is a threat, such as warning that you'll call the police when there's no real reason. Manipulation is scaring or misleading someone, like saying they'll certainly die tonight when you can't know that. Both are unethical, even when your goal is the patient's own good; the end doesn't justify the means.
slides.sayZh: 有时明显需要去医院的病人说「不」，你得去沟通。这里有一条伦理界线。劝说没问题：真诚的关心和理由，比如「你的血压让我担心，如果今天能让医生看看，我会放心很多」。胁迫是威胁，比如在没有真正理由时警告说要叫警察。操纵是吓唬或误导，比如说他今晚肯定会死，而你根本无法确定。两者都不合乎伦理，即使你的目的是为了病人好；目的不能证明手段正当。

slides.title: When the patient can't decide
slides.body:
• Advance directive: wishes stated earlier; used only once incapable
  • Book: the most recent wish counts; BC: must be written, signed, witnessed
  • BC: a representation agreement names a decision maker
  • An executor or financial attorney is not automatically one
  • Substitute decision maker: patient's known wishes first
  • No known wishes: the patient's best interests, not yours
slides.say: If a patient loses capacity, autonomy still counts, in two ways. One is an advance directive: wishes they expressed earlier, while capable. It only takes effect once they're incapable. The book says the most recent wish counts, even a spoken one; in BC, a legal advance directive must be written, signed while capable, and witnessed. The other is a substitute decision maker: in BC, named in a representation agreement, which is different from a power of attorney, or taken from a legal order starting with the spouse. An executor, or someone with power of attorney for money, doesn't automatically decide health care. The substitute follows the patient's known wishes first; without them, the patient's best interests, not anyone else's values.
slides.sayZh: 病人失去决策能力时，自主仍然重要，体现在两方面。一是预先指示：他在有能力时表达过的意愿。它只在病人失去能力后生效。书里说以最新的意愿为准，口头的也算；在 BC，合法的预先指示必须是书面的，在有能力时签署，并有见证人。二是替代决策者：在 BC，由代理协议（representation agreement）指定，它和授权书（power of attorney）不是一回事；或者按法定顺位产生，从配偶开始。遗嘱执行人或管钱财的授权人，并不自动拥有医疗决定权。替代决策者首先遵循病人已知的意愿；没有的话，就按病人的最佳利益，而不是任何其他人的价值观。

slides.title: End-of-life calls and MAID
slides.body:
• Families may call at the moment of death, unsure what to do
  • Give information and support; never judge the call
  • MAID: a physician or nurse practitioner, at the patient's request
  • Bill C-14 (2016): 18+, grievous and irremediable condition
  • Two independent assessments; informed consent at the time
  • On scene: same professional care; ask how you can help

The book describes the 2016 law; federal MAID rules have since been amended.
slides.say: Many calls involve dying patients. Don't judge a family for calling at the end; they may not know how to check a pulse, or that gasping breaths can last for hours. MAID, medical assistance in dying, means a physician or nurse practitioner, at the patient's request, gives a substance that causes death, or provides one the patient takes. The book describes Bill C fourteen, from two thousand sixteen: public health insurance, age eighteen or older, a grievous and irremediable condition, a voluntary request, informed consent, and two independent assessments. At a MAID scene, respond professionally, follow the patient's wishes, ask how you can help, and call direct medical control if unsure.
slides.sayZh: 很多出车会遇到临终病人。不要因为家属在最后时刻打电话就评判他们；他们可能不会摸脉搏，也不知道濒死喘息可以持续好几个小时。MAID，即医疗协助死亡，指医生或执业护士应病人请求，给予致死的药物，或提供药物让病人自己服用。书里讲的是二〇一六年的 Bill C-14：可享受政府医保、年满十八岁、严重且不可治愈的病况、自愿请求、知情同意，并经两名独立专业人员评估。到了 MAID 现场，照常专业响应，遵从病人的意愿，询问能帮什么忙，拿不准时联系直接医疗指导。

slides.title: Withholding or stopping resuscitation
slides.body:
• Futile = the treatment would not work (narrowest meaning)
  • Don't start: obvious death (rigor, lividity, decomposition)
  • Don't start: injuries incompatible with life
  • Stopping may fit: blunt trauma arrest, very long response or effort
  • In doubt? Start, and call direct medical control

A slow code, a show put on for the family, is never ethical.
slides.say: Use the narrowest meaning of futile: a treatment is futile if it would not work, not because someone feels the patient isn't worth it. Treatment may also be withheld or stopped if the patient or substitute asks, if it isn't working or meeting its goals, if burdens outweigh benefits and they agree, or if it's outside accepted prehospital care. Don't start on someone obviously dead, with rigor mortis, lividity or decomposition, or with injuries no one could survive. Stopping may fit a blunt trauma arrest, or a very long response or resuscitation. In doubt, start and call. And never do a slow code: a deliberately weak resuscitation performed for the family.
slides.sayZh: 「无效」要用最窄的定义：治疗不会起作用才叫无效，而不是有人觉得病人「不值得救」。以下情况也可以不开始或停止治疗：病人或替代决策者要求；治疗没起作用或达不到目标；负担大于益处且他们同意；超出公认的院前照护标准。对明显死亡的人，比如有尸僵、尸斑或腐败，或者伤情不可能存活的，不要开始复苏。钝性创伤导致的心脏骤停、响应或复苏时间很长，可能适合停止。有疑问就先开始，再联系医疗指导。绝对不要做慢速抢救，也就是故意做得很弱、演给家属看的复苏。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Verifiable DNR or No CPR order: CPR is contraindicated
  • Adult CPR goes on until advanced care or signs of life, or:
  • 30 min: no ROSC and no shocks
  • 40 min: ROSC at any time, or any shock
  • Stopping the arrest on scene: consult medical oversight
slides.say: In the BC adult CPR protocol, a verifiable Do Not Resuscitate order, or No CPR order, is a contraindication to CPR. Without one, if you're in doubt, you start. Once started, you continue until more advanced providers take over, the patient shows signs of life, or a set time passes: thirty minutes with no ROSC, meaning return of spontaneous circulation, and no shocks; or forty minutes if there was ROSC at any time, or any shock. And the protocol lists stopping a resuscitation on scene as a reason to consult medical oversight. Ethics tells you why; the BC protocol tells you when.
slides.sayZh: BC 成人 CPR 流程中，可核实的 DNR（不复苏）医嘱或 No CPR 医嘱是 CPR 的禁忌。没有这类医嘱、又有疑问时，就开始。一旦开始，就要一直做到更高级别的人员接手、病人出现生命迹象，或到了规定时间：没有 ROSC（自主循环恢复）、也没电击过，三十分钟；任何时候出现过 ROSC，或电击过，四十分钟。流程还把「在现场终止复苏」列为需要咨询医疗监督的情形。伦理告诉你为什么，BC 流程告诉你什么时候。

slides.q: An 85-year-old woman collapsed minutes ago and is in cardiac arrest. Her son says she "never wanted CPR," but there's no DNR or No CPR order. What should you do?
options: Do slow, gentle CPR so the family feels something was tried
Don't start, because the son is her substitute decision maker
Start full resuscitation and contact medical oversight
Wait while the son searches the house for paperwork
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. An eighty-five-year-old woman collapsed minutes ago and is in cardiac arrest. Her son says she never wanted CPR, but there's no DNR or No CPR order. What should you do? A, do slow, gentle CPR so the family feels something was tried. B, don't start, because the son is her substitute decision maker. C, start full resuscitation and contact medical oversight. D, wait while the son searches the house for paperwork. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位八十五岁女士几分钟前倒下，现在心脏骤停。她儿子说她「从来不想做 CPR」，但没有 DNR 或 No CPR 医嘱。你该怎么做？A 做缓慢、轻柔的 CPR，让家属觉得试过了；B 不开始，因为儿子是她的替代决策者；C 开始全力复苏，并联系医疗监督；D 等儿子在家里找文件。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. In the BC CPR protocol, the contraindication is a verifiable DNR or No CPR order, and there isn't one here, so you start. BC also says to consult medical oversight before stopping a resuscitation on scene. A is a slow code, which is never ethical. B is wrong because a spoken report with no verifiable order doesn't meet the BC protocol. D delays CPR when every minute counts; if a valid order turns up, you may stop.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。BC 的 CPR 流程里，禁忌是可核实的 DNR 或 No CPR 医嘱；这里没有，所以要开始复苏。BC 还规定，要在现场终止复苏，须先咨询医疗监督。A 是慢速抢救，任何时候都不合伦理；B 错，只有口头说法、没有可核实的医嘱，不符合 BC 流程；D 在分秒必争时拖延了 CPR；如果之后找到有效医嘱，你可以停止。

slides.title: Harmful orders, organs and research
slides.body:
• An order you believe will harm: never carry it out
  • Explain why; offer an in-scope option or call your medical director
  • Signed donor card? The family still decides
  • Raise donation only under a protocol; never pressure
  • Research: TCPS: respect for persons, concern for welfare, justice
slides.say: Three shorter topics. First, conflicting orders. If a physician asks for a procedure you're not trained for, or a dose far outside your protocol, explain your concern right away. Offer an alternative within your scope, or ask them to speak with your medical director. Never give a treatment you believe will harm the patient; you're their advocate. Second, organ donation: even with a signed donor card, the family decides. Raise donation only if your service has a protocol, and never pressure anyone. Third, research: in Canada, the TCPS, the Tri-Council Policy Statement, rests on respect for persons, concern for welfare, and justice.
slides.sayZh: 三个短话题。第一，医嘱冲突。如果医生要你做没受过训练的操作，或给远超流程范围的剂量，马上说明你的顾虑。提出一个在你执业范围内的替代方案，或请他和你的医疗主管通话。绝不执行你认为会伤害病人的治疗，你是病人的代言人。第二，器官捐献：即使病人签了捐献卡，最终由家属决定。只有机构有相关流程时才提捐献，而且绝不施压。第三，研究：在加拿大，TCPS（Tri-Council Policy Statement，三理事会政策声明）以尊重个人、关注福祉和公正为基础。

slides.title: Accountability: mistakes and misconduct
slides.body:
• Report medical errors, yours or others', to the medical director
  • Never hide a mistake or destroy a record
  • Family asks? Facts only, no guessing: "I'll find out"
  • Report misconduct up the chain of command; protect the reporter
  • Falsified training or certification: licence loss, even criminal charges
  • Sensitive details: phone, not radio
slides.say: Accountability means you own your actions, all the time. If you make a medical error, or see one, report it to your medical director as soon as possible; hiding a mistake can endanger the patient. If a family member asks what went wrong, don't lie and don't guess. Give the facts you know and promise to find out the rest. Don't stay silent about a colleague's misconduct either: report it through your chain of command, and protect the identity of whoever told you. Falsifying training or certification can cost a licence and bring criminal charges. And send sensitive details, like abuse cases, by phone, not radio.
slides.sayZh: 问责意味着你在任何时候都要为自己的行为负责。自己犯了医疗差错，或看到别人犯了，都要尽快报告医疗主管；隐瞒差错可能危及病人。家属问出了什么问题时，不撒谎、不猜测，只讲你知道的事实，并承诺去查清其余的。对同事的不当行为也不能沉默：要通过指挥链上报，并保护告诉你的人的身份。伪造培训或认证记录可能丢掉执照，甚至面临刑事指控。敏感信息，比如虐待案件，要用电话而不是无线电传递。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
• More treatments = more consent talks, each one informed
  • Explain your drugs' benefits, risks and side effects simply
  • Re-check capacity as treatments get more complex
  • Question an unsafe order; offer an option within PCP scope
  • More drugs = more chances of error: report, never hide
  • Drop habits the evidence no longer supports
slides.say: So how does ethics weigh more on a PCP? You'll have more consent conversations, and each must be informed. For your new drugs, that means explaining the benefits, real risks and side effects, and what happens without them. Because capacity is specific, a patient able to accept oxygen may not be able to weigh a more complex treatment, so reassess. When an order seems unsafe, question it and offer an option within PCP scope. More drugs mean more chances of error, so report mistakes quickly and honestly. And stay evidence-based: some procedures don't help patients, even if they seemed to work before.
slides.sayZh: 那么伦理为什么对 PCP 分量更重？你的同意对话更多，每一次都必须是知情的。对你的新药物来说，就是讲清好处、实际风险和副作用，以及不用会怎样。能力是针对具体事情的，能接受吸氧的病人，不一定有能力权衡更复杂的治疗，所以要重新评估。医嘱看起来不安全时，提出质疑，并给出 PCP 范围内的替代方案。药物越多，出错机会越多，所以出了差错要尽快、诚实地报告。还要坚持循证：有些操作对病人没有帮助，哪怕以前看起来「管用」。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Scaring a patient into an IV or a drug is manipulation
  • Directive vs a newer wish? Don't override it alone: call (BC)
  • An executor or money attorney can't decide health care
  • No verifiable DNR or No CPR order? Start, then call
  • A slow code is never acceptable
  • Your own values must not decide for the patient
slides.say: Now the ethical traps that come with more power. Don't exaggerate risks to push a patient into an IV or a drug; that's manipulation, even if you mean well. The book says a newer wish, expressed while capable, beats an old written directive; in BC, don't override an advance directive on your own: consult CliniCall first. Check who really is the substitute decision maker; an executor or financial attorney isn't automatically one. Without a verifiable DNR or No CPR order, start resuscitation and call. Never fake a resuscitation for the family. And keep your own beliefs out of the patient's decision; respecting a choice you disagree with is part of the job.
slides.sayZh: 下面是权力变大后的伦理陷阱。不要夸大风险逼病人接受静脉或药物，即使出于好意，那也是操纵。书里说，病人在有能力时表达的较新意愿优先于旧的书面指示；在 BC，不要自己推翻预先指示，先咨询 CliniCall。核实谁才是真正的替代决策者，遗嘱执行人或财务授权人并不自动是。没有可核实的 DNR 或 No CPR 医嘱，就开始复苏并联系医疗指导。绝不为家属假装抢救。还要把你自己的信念放在病人的决定之外；尊重你不认同的选择，也是工作的一部分。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Four principles; when stuck, ask what's in the patient's best interest
  2. Valid consent: capable, informed, voluntary; persuade, never coerce
  3. No verifiable DNR: start. No slow codes. Own your errors

Next: Chapter 6, Pathophysiology
slides.say: Let's wrap up. One: autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence and justice give you a framework; when they clash, ask what's in this patient's best interest. Two: valid consent needs a capable patient, enough information, and a free choice. Persuade, but never coerce or manipulate. When the patient can't decide, follow their known wishes, then their best interests. Three: without a verifiable DNR or No CPR order, start resuscitation and call; never do a slow code; and report your mistakes honestly. Next, we start chapter six, pathophysiology: how disease changes the body. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，自主、行善、不伤害、公正给你一个框架；原则冲突时，问什么最符合这位病人的利益。二，有效同意需要有能力的病人、足够的信息和自由的选择。可以劝说，但绝不胁迫或操纵。病人无法决定时，先按他已知的意愿，再按他的最佳利益。三，没有可核实的 DNR 或 No CPR 医嘱，就开始复苏并联系医疗指导；绝不做慢速抢救；诚实报告自己的差错。下节课开始第六章病理生理学：疾病如何改变身体。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
